title: Schema resilience probe and automated rollback policy for FP8/INT8 inference
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create an automated resilience test harness and an operational rollback policy that detects structured-output regressions introduced by FP8/INT8 quantization profiles. The goal is to catch schema conformance regressions and high-risk tokenization errors in function-call outputs during calibration and serving, and to enable a fast automated fallback to a compatible model variant or FP16 path when thresholds are breached.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible test harness that runs calibration sweeps against FP8 and INT8 profiles and reports per-field JSON schema pass rate
Coverage metric that measures schema field presence, type conformance, array length stability, and deterministic vs stochastic differences
Automated alerting rule: trigger when rolling 10-minute schema pass rate drops below 97% for a canary cohort
Rollback automation that routes affected traffic to FP16 or a previously validated quant profile within 10 minutes of breach
Integration with CI: PRs that change quant profiles must run the harness and publish a pass/fail badge
test_plan: 1) Expand randomised structured-output generator to include nested arrays, optional fields, and edge-case numeric ranges
2) Run calibration jobs for both FP8 and INT8 across small, medium, and long context lengths with seed control
3) Collect structured-output from golden FP16 baseline and quantized variants, compute per-field diffs and schema pass rates
4) Add per-batch KPIs to the observability pipeline: schema_pass_rate, median_token_shift, avg_array_length_delta
5) Run long-running canary traffic in staging with automatic rollback hooks wired to routing layer
notes_and_progress: 2026-02-20 - Kickoff: scoped harness and metrics; agreed to reuse existing schema validator library and add coverage instrumentation
2026-02-25 - Prototype generator implemented (seeded deterministic fuzzer) and found early regression: INT8 calibration changed array ordering in 'items' under heavy token truncation
2026-03-02 - Observed schema pass rate: FP16 baseline 99.4%, FP8 97.8, INT8 92.1 on long-context function-call tests (detailed logs in staging dashboard)

2026-03-05 - Proposed mitigations: per-layer calibration clamps, conservative quantization profile for outputs used in function calling, and post-generation schema repair heuristics; discussed trade-offs with PM and runtime team

2026-03-07 - Design review with runtime and console teams. Action items: instrument canary route, add a new alert in Console alerts UI, and add rollback route in smart routing service (PR references below)
2026-03-09 - Implemented basic rollback automation and manual trigger in staging; first end-to-end test passed for a synthetic regression case
2026-03-10 - Blocking: need final approval for alert thresholds and confirmation from infra on failover capacity for FP16 fallback
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automated rollback increases cost (routing to FP16) but reduces customer-visible failures; need to quantify runbook cost vs severity
Tightening calibration clamps may increase latency or tokenization divergence for some workloads; trade-off between schema fidelity and per-token quality
Schema repair heuristics can hide underlying model errors and may mask silent failures if overused
implementation_tasks: ENG: extend schema validator to emit per-field coverage and severity scores
ENG: add deterministic seeded schema fuzzer with sample corpus derived from production prompts
ENG: add calibration sweep job that records per-profile artifacts to artifact store
ENG: add observability metrics and console dashboards for schema stability
ENG: implement routing-layer rollback automation and integrate with canary policies
next_steps: 1) Finalize alert thresholds with SRE and Product by 2026-03-12
2) Run full 48-hour staging canary with traffic replay and measure automatic rollback reliability
3) Publish CI badge requirement for quant-profile PRs and merge runtime PR after smoke tests
